title: MP2T: Use the stream, not the addresses, for reassembly
description:
A frame can have multiple MPEG2 TS packets, and individual TSPs can have
the end of one fragmented higher level packet and the beginning of another.
The higher level packets can have protocols like MPE that set the
address and ports on packet_info for a given frame.

Thus, in order to properly reassemble fragments togther, don't use the
addresses and ports, but do use the stream (conversation + direction) that
assigns the fragment IDs.

notes.body: [mpe_fragments.pcapng](/uploads/36c7cfb683dd08c72a65901c6f4d87c5/mpe_fragments.pcapng) and [68E_12610.912_H_6710.ts.pcapng](/uploads/744a320bdbb8a0cebb0c4d0d8c8094f6/68E_12610.912_H_6710.ts.pcapng) are examples of captures that reassemble correctly with this patch, but not without it. For the former file, look at how the last TS packet in frame 3 (CC=8) is not reassembled with the CC=9 fragment in frame 4 without the patch, but it is with the patch. The latter file has many malformed packet errors without this patch, no expert info errors with it.
